batch_patterns.evidence: Across the five narrative/history passages, the key on inference, purpose and main-idea stems is repeatedly the "doubter or loser comes round / plan is vindicated / someone changes their view" option: 16 "Her view of the posts changed after she saw their effect on trade", 34 "Ottilie later relied on a point Nevin had once raised against her", 36 "How a doubted signalling plan proved its worth", 42 "lost out on an acting role and grew proud", 48 "Una is now happy to let her grandfather guide them both", 12 "Mr. Nyberg had started learning new tablet skills on his own", 25 working people's gifts "then reshaped the collection", 44 Konrad "felt no surprise". In 16, 34 and 36 the competing options are the stay-the-same or trusted-from-the-start versions (34B "Nevin continued to doubt", 34D/36C "trusted/full support at once"), so a student who has learned "the skeptic is won over" can pick the key without reading. Moderate strength: each key is also directly supported by its passage.

Three passages (Lunford posts, Quorndale museum, Netherholt mirrors) share one plot: a 19th-century town problem, an innovator, organised opposition (traders' letter / trustees and minister / council and Nevin Osterfeld), a compromise or half-funded trial, an unplanned success, and the opponent converted (Umber pays for a post; Pendle's attendance unchanged; Nevin climbs the hill). The Una and drama-backdrop stories follow the same disappointment-then-vindication arc. Solving the arc of one passage predicts the main-idea and inference keys of the others; the item-level keys are still sound.
